pages.title: Sleep Calculator — What Time Should I Go to Bed? | SleepCycle
pages.description: Enter your wake-up time and get the best bedtime for 5, 4 or 3 sleep cycles (90 minutes each), plus an extra 9-hour option.
pages.h1: What time should I go to bed?
pages.lead: Tell us when you need to wake up. We work backwards through 90-minute sleep cycles — and add the time it takes you to fall asleep.
bullets: 5 cycles (7.5 h) is the usual recommendation for adults
4 cycles (6 h) if you are short on time
6 cycles (9 h) is listed separately as a recovery option

faq.a: We subtract your fall-asleep time and 90 minutes per cycle from your wake-up time. A 07:00 wake-up with 15 minutes to fall asleep gives 23:15 for 5 cycles.
A sleep cycle averages about 90 minutes, though it ranges from 70 to 120 minutes per person. Waking at the end of a cycle usually feels easier.

pages.title: What Time Should I Go to Bed? Bedtime Calculator | SleepCycle
pages.description: A bedtime calculator built on 90-minute sleep cycles. Pick your alarm time and see the three best times to fall asleep.
pages.h1: What time should I go to bed tonight?
pages.lead: Most bedtime advice ignores the obvious: you cannot control when you fall asleep, only when you get into bed. This calculator subtracts both your wind-down time and whole sleep cycles.
bullets: Works backwards from your alarm
Accounts for the minutes you need to fall asleep
Shows which options have already passed

faq.q: Should I aim for 8 hours or 5 cycles?
faq.a: They are roughly the same (5 cycles = 7.5 hours). The cycle view matters because waking mid-cycle often feels worse than waking 30 minutes earlier.

pages.title: If I Go to Bed Now, What Time Should I Wake Up? | SleepCycle
pages.description: Enter your bedtime and see the best wake-up times for 3, 4 and 5 sleep cycles, including an extra 9-hour recovery option.
pages.h1: If I go to bed now, when should I wake up?
pages.lead: This is the other direction: you know when you are getting into bed, and you want the least painful alarm. We add 90 minutes per cycle to your bedtime.
bullets: Useful when your bedtime is fixed but your morning is not
Shows 3, 4 and 5 cycle options side by side
Adds the time you usually need to fall asleep

faq.q: What if I wake up in the middle of a cycle?
faq.a: You will usually feel groggier. If you wake naturally before the alarm, getting up is often better than going back to sleep for 20 minutes.

pages.title: 90-Minute Sleep Cycle Calculator | SleepCycle
pages.description: Sleep in whole 90-minute cycles instead of round hours. See the exact bedtimes for 3, 4, 5 and 6 cycles.
pages.lead: A sleep cycle moves through light sleep, deep sleep and REM, then briefly surfaces. Aligning your alarm with the end of a cycle is the whole idea behind cycle-based bedtimes.
bullets: 3 cycles = 4.5 hours (short night or nap)
5 cycles = 7.5 hours (typical adult target)
6 cycles = 9 hours (recovery after sleep debt)

faq.a: No. Cycles vary between roughly 70 and 120 minutes and lengthen towards morning. Treat 90 minutes as a planning average, not a guarantee.

faq.q: Do naps follow the same cycle?
faq.a: Short naps of 20 minutes avoid deep sleep entirely, which is why they leave you alert rather than groggy.

pages.title: What Time to Go to Bed for 7 Hours of Sleep | SleepCycle
pages.description: Need exactly 7 hours? See the bedtime that gives you 7 hours in bed after accounting for the time it takes to fall asleep.
pages.h1: What time should I go to bed for 7 hours of sleep?
pages.lead: Seven hours in bed is not seven hours asleep. This page subtracts your fall-asleep time so the number you see is real sleep, not time under the covers.
bullets: Adjustable fall-asleep time (0–30 minutes)
Shows the trade-off between 4 and 5 cycles
Works for any wake-up time

faq.a: Most adults need 7 to 9 hours. Seven is the lower end; if you regularly feel tired, add a cycle rather than cutting sleep further.

pages.title: Night Shift Sleep Calculator | SleepCycle
pages.description: A sleep calculator for night-shift and rotating-shift workers. Plan daytime sleep around 90-minute cycles instead of assuming a 9-to-5 schedule.
pages.lead: Most sleep calculators assume you sleep at night. If you work 22:00–06:00 and sleep at 08:00, the maths is the same — but the timing is not.
bullets: Built for daytime sleep after a night shift
Cycle-based wake-up times, not clock-time guilt
Useful for rotating shifts: recalculate each block

faq.q: How should shift workers split sleep?
faq.a: A common pattern is a 4.5-hour core block (3 cycles) plus a 90-minute nap before the shift. Total sleep matters more than a single long block.

faq.q: Does daylight make daytime sleep worse?
faq.a: Yes. Blackout curtains and an eye mask measurably improve daytime sleep quality; the calculator only handles timing.

pages.title: Jet Lag Sleep Calculator | SleepCycle
pages.description: Plan sleep across time zones. Enter your bedtime in the new zone and get cycle-based wake-up times while your body clock catches up.
pages.lead: After a long flight your body clock is still on the old time zone. The practical fix is to anchor a consistent local bedtime and wake at the end of a cycle.
bullets: Plan sleep in the destination time zone
Keeps a stable local wake time while you adjust
Pairs well with morning light exposure

faq.q: How long does jet lag last?
faq.a: Roughly one day per time zone crossed. Light exposure in the morning and avoiding late caffeine shorten it.
A 20-minute nap is safe. A 90-minute nap can make it harder to fall asleep at the local bedtime.

pages.title: Nap Calculator — 20, 60 or 90 Minute Naps | SleepCycle
pages.description: Choose a nap length and see exactly when to set your alarm. 20 minutes for alertness, 90 for a full cycle.
pages.lead: Nap length decides how you feel afterwards. Twenty minutes keeps you in light sleep; ninety minutes completes a full cycle. Anything in between is where the grogginess lives.
bullets: 20 min: alertness boost, no grogginess
90 min: one full cycle, better for sleep debt
Avoid 40–60 minutes unless you can sleep longer

faq.a: Drink coffee, then nap for 20 minutes. Caffeine peaks as you wake, which is why it feels unusually effective.

pages.title: Calculadora de sueño — ¿A qué hora debo dormir? | SleepCycle
pages.description: Introduce tu hora de despertar y obtén la mejor hora para dormir según 5, 4 o 3 ciclos de sueño de 90 minutos.
pages.lead: Dinos a qué hora necesitas despertarte. Calculamos hacia atrás en ciclos de 90 minutos y sumamos el tiempo que tardas en dormirte.
bullets: 5 ciclos (7,5 h) es la recomendación habitual
4 ciclos (6 h) si vas con prisa
6 ciclos (9 h) aparece aparte como opción de recuperación

faq.q: ¿Cómo se calcula la hora de dormir?
faq.a: Restamos tu tiempo para dormirte y 90 minutos por ciclo a la hora de despertar. Despertar a las 07:00 con 15 minutos para dormirte da 23:15 para 5 ciclos.

pages.title: ¿A qué hora debo dormir esta noche? | SleepCycle
pages.description: Calculadora de hora de dormir basada en ciclos de 90 minutos. Elige tu alarma y mira las tres mejores horas para dormirte.
pages.h1: ¿A qué hora debo dormir esta noche?
pages.lead: No puedes controlar cuándo te duermes, solo cuándo te metes en la cama. Esta calculadora resta tu tiempo de conciliación y ciclos completos.
bullets: Calcula desde tu alarma
Tiene en cuenta los minutos que tardas en dormirte
Marca las opciones que ya han pasado

faq.a: Son casi lo mismo (5 ciclos = 7,5 horas). La diferencia es despertar al final de un ciclo en lugar de en medio.

pages.title: Calculadora de sueño para turno nocturno | SleepCycle
pages.description: Para quienes trabajan de noche: planifica el sueño diurno con ciclos de 90 minutos en lugar de asumir un horario de oficina.
pages.h1: Calculadora de sueño para turno nocturno
pages.lead: Casi todas las calculadoras asumen que duermes de noche. Si trabajas de 22:00 a 06:00 y duermes a las 08:00, la matemática es la misma; el momento no.
bullets: Pensada para el sueño diurno tras el turno
Horas de despertar por ciclos
Útil en turnos rotativos: recalcula cada bloque

faq.a: Un patrón habitual es un bloque principal de 4,5 horas (3 ciclos) más una siesta de 90 minutos antes del turno.
